question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by binary fission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a mode of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two equal and identical daughter cells.
 
• **Amoeba**, a unicellular organism, reproduces by binary fission. During this process, its nucleus divides by mitosis, followed by the division of the cytoplasm, resulting in two identical cells.
 
• Binary fission in Amoeba occurs under favorable conditions such as adequate temperature, moisture, and nutrient availability.
 
• Unlike Amoeba, organisms like **Spirogyra** reproduce through fragmentation, **Hydra** via budding, and **Planaria** through regeneration. Hence, these organisms do not reproduce by binary fission.
 
• Binary fission ensures the rapid multiplication of organisms, allowing them to adapt quickly to favorable environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amoeba:**

 
 
• Amoeba is a **unicellular protozoan** that belongs to the kingdom Protista.
 
• It is found in freshwater, soil, and marine environments.
 
• The organism has an irregular shape and moves using temporary projections of its cytoplasm called **pseudopodia**.
 
• Amoeba can survive harsh conditions by forming a **protective cyst**, a process known as encystation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission:**
 
 
• Binary fission is a simple and efficient mode of asexual reproduction commonly observed in prokaryotes like bacteria and some eukaryotes like Amoeba and Paramecium.
 
• It involves three main steps: replication of the genetic material, elongation of the cell, and division into two daughter cells.
 
• There are different types of binary fission based on the plane of division: **simple binary fission** (irregular plane, seen in Amoeba), **transverse binary fission** (horizontal plane, seen in Paramecium), and **longitudinal binary fission** (vertical plane, seen in Euglena).
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra:**
 
 
• Spirogyra is a **filamentous green alga** that reproduces mainly through fragmentation and sexual reproduction (conjugation).
 
• In fragmentation, each broken filament develops into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Hydra:**
 
 
• Hydra reproduces asexually through **budding**, where a small outgrowth (bud) develops on the parent body and eventually detaches to become an independent organism.
 
 
 
• **Planaria:**
 
 
• Planaria exhibits **regeneration**, where it can regrow lost body parts or develop into a complete organism from a small fragment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Binary fission vs Other Modes of Asexual Reproduction:**

 
 
• **Binary fission:** A parent cell splits into two equal halves (e.g., Amoeba).
 
• **Budding:** A small bud forms on the parent organism and detaches (e.g., Hydra).
 
• **Fragmentation:** The organism breaks into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new organism (e.g., Spirogyra).
 
• **Regeneration:** The ability of an organism to regrow lost parts or form a new organism from fragments (e.g., Planaria).
